01

About

After graduating from San Francisco State University in International Business, I dove headfirst into the startup world at Mango Leopard, managing a 22,000-unit supply chain portfolio across international freight corridors, coordinating shipments from Bangladesh, racing against deadlines, and learning what it actually means to run operations under pressure.

But the more I worked, the more I realized something: I could see the problems clearly. I just didn't always have the tools to solve them at the depth they deserved. I was making decisions with gut instinct and spreadsheets when the situation was calling for something more rigorous, more precise.

"I wasn't lacking ambition or work ethic. I was missing a language: the language of data, of models, of turning uncertainty into strategy. So I decided to learn it properly."

I applied to Johns Hopkins Carey Business School, and was admitted with a scholarship. Now I approach every problem with both the operational instincts I built in the field and the analytical rigor to back them up.

PROJECT // 01
AI Product · Founder Intelligence
New Founders
AI-Powered Founder Discovery Platform
1Problem

Investors struggle to identify promising non-traditional founders, technically strong builders without a prior track record, since standard sourcing surfaces mostly established profiles. New Founders pulls live public signal to help investors spot overlooked technical talent earlier.

2Data
  • Live GitHub developer activity signals
  • Semantic Scholar research/publication data
  • Relational persistence layer for session context
3Approach
  • Weighted multi-axis AI scoring engine (Founder/Market/Idea/Trust)
  • LLM-synthesized analysis stored for context-aware retrieval
  • Trust/claims verification system with minimum threshold gate
  • Built on TanStack Start, TypeScript, and Supabase PostgreSQL
4Insights
  • Weighting: 40% Founder quality · 30% Market opportunity · 20% Idea-market fit · 10% Trust
  • Surfaces first-time/non-traditional builders standard sourcing misses
  • Verification gate reduces false or unverifiable founder claims
  • Deployed live and accessible to investors today

PROJECT // 02
Python · Data Analysis
Fuel Inventory Intelligence
Cost Optimization Across a Gas Station Network
1Problem

A regional Canadian fuel network across 8 stations had no systematic inventory strategy. Replenishment cycles ranged wildly from 0.7 to 33 days, causing frequent stockouts and 2,500+ transactions that missed tiered volume discount thresholds, leaving significant savings on the table.

2Data
  • 5 datasets merged on tank_id
  • 1,859,658 fuel-level records
  • 2,831 cleaned invoices
3Approach
  • Built unified 1.86M+ row analytical dataset
  • Tiered discount model + IQR outlier filtering
  • Safety stock + reorder point optimization
  • 5-year NPV cost-benefit analysis per station
4Insights
  • Thursday = statistically optimal buy day
  • 8–12% projected annual cost reduction identified
  • Station 1 highest NPV candidate (~$124K)
  • Recommended consolidated purchasing strategy

PROJECT // 03
Healthcare Analytics · Consulting
ACHP Medicare Advantage Analysis
Market Exit Intelligence for National Health Plan Association
1Problem

607 Medicare Advantage plans exited the market across 43 states in 2025–2026, displacing thousands of beneficiaries. ACHP, a national health plan association, needed to identify which markets they won, which they lost, and where to act before the next open enrollment window.

2Data
  • CMS MA Landscape CY2025 & 2026
  • 607 plans · 43 states · 1,268 counties
  • Monthly enrollment 2025–2026
3Approach
  • Full CMS data pipeline + feature engineering
  • 3 hypotheses tested (p < 0.0001)
  • HHI market concentration modeling
  • Expand vs Defend county triage framework
4Insights
  • +0.82pp share gain in exit counties vs +0.28pp elsewhere
  • Product vacuum (not exit volume) drives pickup
  • 185 Expand counties · 73 Defend counties flagged
  • Presented early-warning system to ACHP leadership
PythonCMS DataHHI

PROJECT // 04
Operations Research · Stochastic LP
BaaS Nairobi: Battery-as-a-Service
Two-Stage Stochastic LP with Tiered SLA Penalties
1Problem

A 50-unit residential complex in Nairobi needed to replace unreliable diesel backup power with a 200 kWh Li-ion battery system. The core challenge: when to charge and when to discharge, given Kenya's time-of-use electricity tariffs and unpredictable grid outages?

2Data
  • KPLC tariffs: $0.15–$0.25/kWh
  • 3 World Bank outage scenarios
  • 200 kWh Li-ion battery
3Approach
  • Two-stage stochastic LP with non-anticipativity
  • Tiered SLA: Premium (40%) vs Basic (60%)
  • 3 outage scenarios from World Bank data
  • Cross-validated: Python/Gurobi + Excel Solver
4Insights
  • Optimal expected daily cost: $107.96
  • VSS = $13.86 (cost of ignoring uncertainty)
  • Zero unserved Premium energy across all scenarios
  • Charge off-peak ($0.15), discharge peak ($0.25)
PythonGurobiStochastic LP

PROJECT // 05
Predictive Modeling · R Studio
Digital Behavior & Mental Wellness
Predicting Stress from Social Media Usage Patterns
1Problem

With rising mental health concerns tied to screen time, this project used 5,000 survey responses to identify which digital platforms and usage patterns most strongly predict stress, and built a classifier to deliver precise, threshold-based digital hygiene recommendations.

2Data
  • 5,000 survey responses
  • Platform hours, device, sleep metrics
  • Mixed numeric & categorical in R
3Approach
  • Multiple linear regression: R² = 0.93
  • KNN classifier (92.5% accuracy)
  • Decision Tree classifier (96.6% accuracy)
  • K-Means clustering (k=3) for user segmentation
4Insights
  • Social media is dominant stress driver above 3.85h/day
  • 3 user personas: Low-risk, At-risk, High-risk
  • Decision Tree outperforms KNN by 4.1pp
  • Sleep quality mediates the usage-stress relationship
R StudioKNNK-Means

PROJECT // 06
Marketing Analytics · Linear Programming
MirWork Marketing Optimization
LP Budget Allocation & Risk-Adjusted Decision Analysis
1Problem

MirWork needed to allocate a $7,000 advertising budget across three platforms to maximize conversions, while also deciding whether to run campaigns in-house or outsource. Both decisions required balancing expected returns against downside risk.

2Data
  • Platform conversion benchmarks
  • Revenue & cost scenarios modeled
  • Probability-weighted outcomes
3Approach
  • Linear program via Excel Solver across 3 platforms
  • Decision tree with probability-weighted EV
  • Scenario analysis: best, base, worst case
  • Risk-adjusted comparison: in-house vs outsourced
4Insights
  • Both options yield EV = $46K: risk is the differentiator
  • In-house worst case: –$10K vs outsourced: –$50K
  • LP optimized: 42% LinkedIn, 35% Instagram, 23% TikTok
  • Recommended in-house for 5x better downside protection
